title: A one-week automated genome-wide optical pooled screen using OttoSeq.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: BioImage Archive S-BIAD3096 metadata and FTP listing: 150,480 files, about 2.8 TiB of raw TIFF microscopy images (input_ph/, input_sbs/ folders, plate_1 and plate_2) plus file_list.json/tsv, licence CC0. GitHub repo cheeseman-lab/whitney-analysis: opened significant_genes.tsv (3,716 rows, one 'gene' column mixing symbols, Ensembl IDs and non-targeting controls), essential_genes.tsv (5,049 symbols), cluster_genes_table.tsv (566 rows x 14 columns of LLM cluster annotations). Read brieflow_output_report.md (5,198,240 cells, 21,732 perturbations, median 224 cells/gene, 794 PC features) and deployment scripts showing the per-gene aggregate feature TSVs (~1.8 GB) live on a lab server / private Google Cloud bucket, not in any public archive.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Supplementary Tables S2-S4 (coverage and cluster assignments); the supplement endpoint timed out and was not retrieved. Whether the Streamlit viewer (whitney.broadinstitute.org) lets users download per-gene profiles was not verified; it is a JavaScript app that returned no data.

a1_downloadable.note: Raw images are public under CC0 at BioImage Archive (verified listing); processed per-gene and per-cell feature tables are not deposited anywhere public (verified via repo scripts pointing to private paths).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No per-gene phenotype table is public. The only gene-level label is a 3,716-row hit list (significant_genes.tsv); negatives would have to be constructed from the library file, and any richer morphological label requires re-running the Brieflow image pipeline.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genes are named by symbol or Ensembl ID (verified), so protein or gene embeddings would be a standard lookup.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable for a binary hit label; features would be normalised CellProfiler-style measurements per the report.

a5_enough_rows.note: 3,716 hit rows verified (including some non-targeting controls), out of ~21,730 genes per the pipeline report.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Getting any quantitative per-gene phenotype means reprocessing 2.8 TiB of images with segmentation (Cellpose) and barcode calling; that needs a cluster, not a 16 GB laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Pipeline report numbers (5,198,240 cells, 21,732 perturbations, 3,715 significant genes, 320 clusters) match the abstract.

a8_label_provenance.note: Hit calls come from bootstrap statistics on measured Cell Painting features, not another model; the cluster pathway labels, however, are LLM (Claude) annotations and would be circular.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) for gene-level input embeddings, if the profiles were public

integration.partner_dataset: DepMap gene essentiality; CORUM / STRING complexes (benchmark files already in repo)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could protein sequence predict which knockouts change HeLa morphology beyond what essentiality already explains? Not pursued because the profiles are not public.

controls.positive_control: Essential genes (5,049-gene reference list in repo) should be enriched among hits.
controls.external_validation: Other genome-wide optical pooled screens (e.g. Funk et al. 2022 HeLa screen); not checked here.

honest_claim_h3: At best: predicts whether knocking out a gene produced a detectable Cell Painting change in one HeLa screen, a label strongly confounded with essentiality.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a gene's protein sequence to predict whether knocking it out visibly changes cell shape and organelle staining in human cells.
plain_idea.train_on: One example per gene (about 21,730 genes, from the pipeline report), described by a protein sequence embedding.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the knockout was called a significant morphological hit (3,716-row list verified), from microscopy of 5.2 million barcoded HeLa cells.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would prioritise genes for imaging screens, but the binary label is thin and mostly tracks essentiality; the rich per-gene profiles that would make it worthwhile are not public.

ml_idea: Predict per-gene morphological profiles or hit status from protein/gene embeddings; blocked because only raw images (2.8 TiB) and a binary hit list are public.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only: rebuilding per-gene features means segmenting ~34,000 image tiles from 2.8 TiB raw data, cluster-scale work.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Email the authors or inspect the Streamlit viewer for a downloadable per-gene aggregate TSV (~1.8 GB); if none, the project is dead.

verdict_reason: Public deposit is 2.8 TiB of raw images only; the per-gene feature tables (~1.8 GB) sit on a private lab bucket, and the only public label is a 3,716-gene hit list, so a usable label table would have to be rebuilt from images (fails A2 and A6). Revisit if the aggregate profiles get deposited.
